rescore_meta.rescore_note: All seven re-score m-sources corroborate or extend the original SHORT thesis. The original 2-recall openFDA finding under-counted by 3 — there are at least FIVE Prestige-branded FDA recalls in 2022-2025 (Class I: TING 2% Miconazole 12/2023, TING 1% Tolnaftate 2/2024, Americaine benzene 1/2024; Class II: TheraTears Extra 3/2022, Clear Eyes olopatadine 3/2023, Little Remedies Gas Relief 6/2024, Little Remedies Honey Cough 7/2025). NONE of these are named in the FY2026 10-K's product-liability section. The Foundation Consumer Brands BDC-debt trace is the MOST IMPORTANT new finding — it lets us anchor the implied cost of PBH's pending $1.2B term loan at ~8-9%, vs. PBH's existing 3.75% 2021 notes ($600M, callable 4/1/26) that must also refinance. Pro-forma interest expense step-up = ~$50-70M/yr (5% rate Δ × $1B+ refinanced/new debt) — a 15-22% drag on FY2026 net income of $190M. Composite INCREASED 1.33 -> 1.60 (capped at SHORT-tier conviction).

rfm_tuples.M_value: FIVE confirmed Prestige-branded FDA recalls in the 2022-2025 window, none named in the FY2026 10-K: (1) 2022-03-30 Class II TheraTears Extra (sodium carboxymethylcellulose) — manufactured by Akorn Inc — 'Lack of Assurance of Sterility' (sterile-eye-care issue, identical category to current Clear Eyes shortage); (2) 2023-03-22 Class II Clear Eyes Once Daily Eye Allergy Itch Relief (olopatadine) — manufactured by Teva Pharmaceuticals — 'Failed Impurities Specification, OOS stability test results'; (3) 2023-12-27 Class I TING 2% Miconazole Nitrate Athlete's Foot Spray (Insight Pharmaceuticals) — benzene contamination; (4) 2024-01-24 Class I Americaine Benzocaine 20% Topical Anesthetic Spray (Insight Pharmaceuticals) — benzene contamination; (5) 2024-02-28 Class I TING 1% Tolnaftate Athlete's Foot Spray (Insight Pharmaceuticals) — benzene contamination; (6) 2024-06-26 Class II Little Remedies Gas Relief Drops (Simethicone) — manufactured by Denison Pharmaceuticals — 'cGMP deviations, atypical Burkholderia Cepacia'; (7) 2025-07-23 Class II Little Remedies Honey Cough — recalling firm 'Prestige Brands Holdings' DIRECTLY — 'Bacillus cereus contamination, may be spoiled.' Total = 3 Class I + 4 Class II in 40 months across at least 4 Prestige-branded product lines.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The original score caught the 2 most severe (Class I, 2024) but materially under-counted: there is a SUSTAINED recall pattern across MULTIPLE Prestige brands and at least THREE contract manufacturers (Insight Pharmaceuticals, Akorn, Denison Pharmaceuticals, Teva). The 2025-07-23 Little Remedies Honey Cough recall is filed under 'Prestige Brands Holdings' as the recalling firm — meaning the issuer itself is now directly named on FDA enforcement actions, not just a subsidiary. The 2022 TheraTears sterility failure is especially telling because it foreshadows the current Clear Eyes sterile-eye-care 'industry shortage' narrative — PBH had a sterile-eye-care manufacturing-quality event in 2022 that it now repackages as exogenous industry headwinds in 2026. Mode B catch: the 10-K's 'routine matters' framing is contradicted by a 40-month pattern of FDA enforcement spanning 5 distinct Prestige brands.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode B (Investigator add-on) — verify Foundation Consumer Brands' standalone credit profile by tracing it through public BDC 10-Q schedules of investments. rfm_tuples.M_value: Foundation Consumer Brands LLC appears as a portfolio loan holding in at least 4 SLR Capital Partners affiliated BDCs (SCP Private Credit Income BDC, SLR Investment Corp, SLR HC BDC, SLR Private Credit BDC II). Existing senior secured loan terms disclosed in SLR Private Credit BDC II's 3/31/2026 10-Q: classification = 'Bank Debt/Senior Secured Loans', spread = SOFR + 500 bps, floor = 1.00%, all-in yield = 8.80-9.09%, origination = January 2025, maturity = February 2029, principal $1,255K position at cost $1,250K, fair value $1,255K (essentially at par). The loan is held across multiple SLR vehicles consistent with a club-syndicated unitranche. Implication for PBH's takeout: PBH will need to issue $1.2B+ of new term loan debt to fund the Foundation acquisition. Given (a) PBH is investment-grade-adjacent (BB/Ba) vs Foundation's sub-IG private-credit borrower profile, PBH should price somewhat tighter; but (b) PBH's existing 2021 Senior Notes at 3.75% ($600M, callable 4/1/26) and 2019 Senior Notes at 5.125% ($400M, mature 1/15/28) must both refinance in 2026-2028, AND (c) the new $1.2B Foundation term loan is incremental. Reasonable pro-forma blended rate post-deal = 6.5-8.0% on $2.2B vs current ~4.3% blended on $1.0B. Pro-forma interest expense step-up estimate: $2.2B × 7% = $154M vs current $1.0B × 4.3% = $43M, a delta of $111M/yr pre-tax (or $85M after-tax at 23% — a 45% drag on FY2026 net income of $190M).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch. The 10-K discloses the leverage jump but not the rate-step-up math. By tracing the seller's existing debt through public BDC schedules, we anchor the implied takeout rate at ~8-9% — and PBH has TWO concurrent refinance walls (3.75% 2021 notes callable now, 5.125% 2026 notes mature 1/2028). The unstated cash interest expense impact post-Foundation is in the $100M+/yr range, which materially impairs the deal's accretion narrative. The 10-K frames Foundation as 'accretive in the first full year post-close' without disclosing the rate-environment refinance overlay. This is the single most material non-form4 m-source finding in the re-score.
